input.brief: Fan-made concept site for Stuff Made Here, Shane Wighton's engineering channel: machines that won't let you miss

direction.name: Type and nothing else
direction.idea: The first screen is made only of words, colour and space, good enough that nobody misses a picture there. Pictures arrive later, large and few, as relief from the type. This is the honest answer when a subject has nothing worth photographing: instead of inventing illustrations, set what you have to say as well as it can be set. The typography carries a point of view through scale (one enormous statement, everything else small), through measure (a narrow, bookish column or a full-width line), and through one committed colour.
direction.composition: First screen: the statement, two lines at most, set at 9–14vw and occupying the full width with tight leading, positioned in the upper two-thirds. One supporting sentence at 20–24px sits bottom-left on the same margin and the single action sits bottom-right on the same baseline. No navigation bar; two or three links in a top corner. Sections that follow are typographic set pieces, each different: a list of five to eight capabilities set at 4–6vw one per line; a paragraph at 28–36px in a 28ch column pushed to the right half; a pair of large numerals with a sentence each; a single quotation filling a colour field. Each section uses a different horizontal position (left, right, full) so the page has movement without imagery.
direction.typography: This direction lives or dies on the face and its settings. Display at tight tracking and leading; text sizes few and far apart (for example 15, 22, 34 and the display size). Use real typographic detail: proper quotes, balanced line breaks, hung punctuation where it helps.
direction.colour: Either one saturated ground for the whole page with a single ink, or paper and ink with one section inverted and one in the accent as a full field. Colour does the job images would have done.
direction.imagery: The first screen has no picture. Further down, real pictures of the subject's world (found with scripts/assets.mjs) arrive large and few: a full-bleed photograph between two type sections, a looping clip in one band, an archival image beside a list. Do not add icons, shapes, patterns or abstract graphics to compensate for anything.
direction.richness: Scale contrast and colour mass. A capability list set at 5vw is an image in its own right.
direction.pitfalls: Without pictures, weak copy has nowhere to hide: write real sentences. Vary the set pieces; four sections of big-heading-plus-paragraph is a text document, not a design. Keep all headings within two lines.

hero.name: Two-line statement, full width
hero.blueprint: Paper and ink only; no image. The wordmark at 15px sits top-left and two or three text links at the same size top-right, both on 24px margins; there is no bar. The statement fills the upper two thirds: two lines at clamp(96px, 12.5vw, 200px), medium to bold weight, tracking -0.05em, leading 0.86, starting 15% below the top edge. The first line is flush to the left margin and the second flush to the right margin, so the pair spans the full width and steps across the screen. Size the type so the longer line runs margin to margin: tune the vw value to the character count and test it at 1440 and 390. Between the statement and the bottom row about 18% of the height is left empty. The bottom row sits on one baseline 28px above the bottom edge: one supporting sentence at 22px on the left, max 44ch on two lines, and the single action bottom-right as a solid ink rectangle with square corners. There is no colour beyond ground and ink.
hero.mobile: Both lines turn flush left on 16px margins at 17vw, leading 0.9, starting at 14% of the height and filling the width. A gap of about 20% of the screen follows. The sentence sits at 17px above a full-width action, both anchored to the bottom with 20px to spare. Navigation reduces to the wordmark and one menu word.
hero.headline: A 3-5 word statement on two lines, at most 11 characters per line so 17vw type fits a phone.

type.note: A black grotesque in capitals with letters nearly colliding, and only two sizes on the page: enormous and small. Suits agencies, city and culture projects and musicians who want the type to land like a headline.

palette.name: Navy and pink
palette.note: One navy field runs the entire page. Pink does everything else, from the name and headings to body text, and fills one solid button.

motion.name: Masked headline
motion.description: On load, each line of the headline rises from behind its own baseline, about 900ms with a strong ease-out, the second line 110ms after the first; the supporting sentence and the action then fade up together. Nothing else on the page performs. Because headlines are two lines at most, you author the line breaks and wrap each line yourself. Recipe: 'Masked line reveal' in references/motion.md.

sections.name: Object in front of type
sections.blueprint: Type and object share one space instead of sitting side by side. Three or four lines of display type, one or two words each, are stacked flush left at clamp(72px, 9vw, 150px) with leading 0.88, starting on the left margin and allowed to leave the right edge (white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden on the section). The lines step through tones of one ink: one at 45%, one at full strength, the rest at 18%. The object photograph, a cut-out or a studio shot blended with multiply, is absolutely positioned over the upper right of the stack at 40–46vw wide, rotated no more than 6 degrees and above the type in the stacking order, so it hides parts of three or four letters. Under the stack, in columns 8–12, a two-paragraph block at 20px gives the facts. The full-strength line is the heading; nothing sits above it.
sections.mobile: Type drops to 15vw and still runs off the right edge. The object sits at 78vw wide, overlapping the last two lines from below instead of from the right, and is cropped by the right edge. The facts block follows at full width and 17px.

sections.name: Quiet ledger, side preview
sections.blueprint: A plain ledger in one column 560px wide whose left edge sits at 22% of the viewport width. A heading of two or three words at 24–28px in medium weight, then 32px of space, then one row per project, 44px tall: the name at 16px in full ink at the left, the kind of work at 14px in the soft ink starting at 55% of the column, and the year right-aligned with tabular figures. Nothing is drawn between rows; the three fixed starts make the columns. Hovering or focusing a row keeps it in full ink, drops the others to the soft ink, and shows that project's image in the empty area right of the column: a 4:3 frame 300px wide, `position: absolute`, its top aligned to the hovered row, 64px from the column's right edge, appearing with a 150ms fade. Holds 6–20 rows; group by year with 28px of extra space.
sections.mobile: The column fills the width with 20px margins. Rows are 52px tall: name at the left, year at the right, kind of work on a second line at 13px. There is no hover preview; instead the first three projects each show a 16:10 image at full column width above their row.

sections.name: Itinerary on a slip
sections.blueprint: The process is printed as an itinerary or receipt. One paper-coloured slip 420–480px wide stands on a contrasting flat ground at columns 7–11; its bottom edge is a zigzag cut with clip-path and its top edge is straight. The heading, two to four words at clamp(40px, 4.4vw, 68px), sits in columns 1–5 with a 30ch paragraph, top-aligned with the slip. On the slip, in the text face at 16px with tabular figures: stages grouped under time headings that carry the order ('Monday', 'Midweek', 'Friday'), each heading in bold with 28px above it. Under a heading, two to four rows; each row has what happens on the left, a duration or time on the right, and a leader of round 4px dots between. The final row is inverted, paper-coloured text on a full-width ink bar 44px tall, and states the result: what the reader holds at the end and the total time.
sections.mobile: The heading and paragraph come first. The slip follows at full width minus 16px margins, keeping its zigzag bottom edge. Rows keep left text, dots and right value on one line; long descriptions wrap under the left text. The inverted final row stays full width.

sections.name: Wall of word tiles
sections.blueprint: A gallery that works with no photographs: a four-column grid of identical square cells with 8px gaps running three or more rows, edge to edge with 8px margins. Each cell is a flat filled tile and centres one large element about 55% of the cell's width: a single word, a letter, a figure with its unit, or a simple inline SVG shape taken from the subject, set at clamp(56px, 9vw, 150px) in the display face. A one- or two-word caption at 14px sits centred 18px above the cell's bottom edge. Tile and ink colours rotate through three or four palette pairs in a fixed order, so a uniform grid looks varied. Where photographs exist, every third or fourth cell is a photograph covering its tile, all given one treatment. There is no hierarchy between cells: it is a specimen sheet. A heading is optional; if used, it occupies the first cell as that cell's word.
sections.mobile: Two columns with 6px gaps; cells stay square and the central element is set at 22vw. Captions stay at 13px. Twelve cells make six rows; if there are more than sixteen, show twelve and let the rest follow after a full-width tile holding a text link.

sections.name: Two columns, highlighted words
sections.blueprint: The story is set as text far larger than anything else on the page: 110–160 words at clamp(22px, 2.1vw, 32px), tight leading 1.18, in the soft ink, flowing through two columns that fill the full width between 24px margins (`columns: 2; column-gap: 32px`, justified, with hyphenation on). No heading. The name at the start is in full ink. Six or seven single words or short phrases carry a flat highlighter background in three or four palette colours, built with an inline `background-color`, `box-decoration-break: clone` and 0.1em of horizontal padding; they mark the facts a scanning reader wants (a place, a year, a client, a skill). The final short sentence is highlighted entire in the strongest colour and is the link to contact. Padding 120px top and bottom. No image and no portrait.
sections.mobile: One column at 20px, left-aligned and unjustified, leading 1.25, with 18px margins. Keep four or five highlights so no line carries two. The final highlighted sentence sits on its own line with 24px above it and works as a full-width tap target.

sections.name: One word is the button
sections.blueprint: The entire band is one link. A full-bleed field in the accent colour, about 60svh tall, contains a single verb of four to eight letters set at 24–30vw in the heaviest weight, tight tracking, sized with `clamp()` so it spans the content width on one line with its baseline 24px above the bottom edge. The `<a>` wraps the whole band; on hover and focus the field and the word swap colours instantly. In the top-left corner, at 20px, one sentence says what happens next; in the top-right, an arrow drawn as a simple inline SVG, 48px, points up and right. There is no other button anywhere in the section. In a page with a motif, the band's top corners take the motif's shape (a large radius, or a chamfer cut with `clip-path`). Keep the word honest: the action itself, not a slogan.
sections.mobile: The band is 46svh tall. The word is set at whatever size fills the width on one line; choose a shorter verb rather than going below 22vw. Sentence top-left at 17px across two lines, arrow top-right at 32px. The whole band stays tappable.

sections.name: Columns above, wordmark below
sections.blueprint: The footer inverts ground and ink and fills a whole viewport (min-height 100svh), arranged as three rows in a grid (auto 1fr auto). Top row, 40px from the edge: four small columns on the 12-column grid (address, navigation, social, hours or contact), each a plain list at 15–16px with its first line in the full ink and the rest in the softer ink. Middle row: empty. Bottom row: the wordmark alone, sized to run from the left margin to the right margin on one line. Set it as inline SVG text with a `viewBox` fitted to the word and `width: 100%`, or tune `font-size` in `vw` to the letter count, so it never wraps; its baseline sits 20px above a single line of legal text at 13px. With `position: sticky; bottom: 0` and a lower `z-index` than the page, the last section slides away to uncover it.
sections.mobile: Columns become two by two at 15px with 32px between rows, at the top. A gap of about 20svh follows. The wordmark spans the full width at the bottom; a name longer than ten letters stacks on two lines, each fitted to the width. Legal line beneath at 12px.

references.name: NOTHIN’
references.idea: The studio's name set as a wordmark so large it is the whole hero, repeated in inverted colours as the footer, so 'nothing' is literally the only content on screen.
references.hero: The captured hero frame is a black preloader wipe; this describes the loaded state. White field. A custom heavy geometric wordmark in black spans the full width between 1% margins, vertically centred, about 30% of the viewport tall, its apostrophe hanging at the top-right. Top-left: a two-line statement at about 1.6vw with a small black pill button under it. Top-right: a tiny menu label with a four-dot icon. Along the bottom edge: a one-line studio descriptor at left, two social links and a language chip at right. Everything else is empty white, with no image and no colour.
references.type: PP Neue Montreal medium for statements at up to about 5vw, sentence case, tight tracking and leading; the Book cut for small text; IBM Plex Mono for tiny grey project labels. The wordmark is custom heavy geometric lettering at close to 100vw. Only three text sizes: statement, caption, micro-label.
references.colour: #ffffff #000000 #2b47e6 #2f5d33 #bfbfbf — Strict black and white that flips by section: white hero and intro, black works and footer. The only colour comes from inside the imagery, chiefly electric-blue foil and fern green.
references.imagery: 3D renders of inflated chrome, crumpled blue foil and bubble-wrap hearts on black; project shots are brand mock-ups photographed in settings (a card among ferns, a laptop on a dark desk). Hard-edged rectangles of varied size, square corners.
references.layout: Margins of about 1%, so content runs nearly edge to edge. The intro is a left headline over a full-width black media panel; the works section places images at irregular widths and horizontal offsets with wide black gaps, each with a mono label and one-line caption above.

sections.description: White section. A two-line statement at about 5vw sits flush left under a small logo mark, filling the top quarter. Below it a black rectangle spans the full content width and runs off the bottom of the viewport, holding a 3D still life clustered at centre. On further scroll the panel shrinks to a small thumbnail docked top-right, while a parenthesised label and a four-line paragraph at caption size appear in two narrow columns at the left.

Black section headed by one bold uppercase word top-left. Project images are placed as a loose scatter: one at about 48% width hugging the left margin, the next narrow and hugging the right margin lower down, the next inset to start 18% across. Above each image sits a tiny grey mono project name, then a one-line white caption at about 1.1vw. A two-line aphorism floats alone at the right between projects. Long stretches of empty black separate items.

Black, full viewport. A two-line invitation at about 5vw at the left in the upper third, with two outlined pill buttons under it; three social links stacked at about 78% across. The wordmark repeats in white at full width, anchored to the bottom, with a single row of micro-text credits beneath it.

steal: Make the hero nothing but the name: a wordmark scaled to the full viewport width on a blank field, with only a two-line statement and one small button in a corner.
Repeat the hero wordmark in inverted colours as the footer so the page opens and closes on the same shape.
Place case-study images at different widths and horizontal offsets on a black field, each with a micro mono label and a single-line caption above it instead of a card.

references.name: bleibtgleich’26
references.idea: One thin vertical rule runs down the page and a tight bold grotesk sentence wraps around it, words stepping from one side of the line to the other.
references.hero: White page, black type. Content sits in a narrow band between 26% and 68% of the width. A 1px vertical rule drops from the top edge at 37% for two-thirds of the height. Left of it: a black blob avatar at the top, a tiny role caption at its foot. Right of it: a tiny location note at the top, the name in two lines of 90px medium grotesk at the bottom. The tagline continues below at the same size, flush to the band's left edge, running past the fold. The upper half is otherwise blank. The handle is split into two pale-grey words fixed in the bottom corners; a black menu pill sits top-right.
references.type: Akzidenz Grotesk Pro medium only, -0.05em tracking, line-height about 0.9. Two sizes: 90px (6.3vw) for every statement and 11-13px for captions and table rows, a 7:1 jump. Long words are hyphenated and stepped across lines on purpose.
references.colour: #ffffff #000000 #e4e4e4 #f2f2f2 — Black on white with no accent. Pale grey is used for the ghosted corner wordmark and a few small square tiles; tiny coloured rings inside those tiles are the only hue.
references.imagery: Almost none: a black blob avatar, a few 85px grey tiles each with a coloured ring, and a canvas dome of small tilted project thumbnails floating between two words.
references.layout: Everything hangs off one vertical axis at 37%: lines start either at the axis or one indent to its left, giving a stepped rag. Very wide white margins. Sections are separated by a full screen of white rather than rules or colour.

sections.description: A 90px sentence is typeset word by word around the vertical rule: one word ends just left of the rule, the next starts just right of it, and the following line is centred beneath both. Above the sentence a row of five 85px pale-grey squares, each with a small coloured ring at its centre, is spaced unevenly along one baseline, with a three-line 13px description under the second.

The heading first appears as one centred line near the bottom of an empty screen, then its two halves separate to the far left and far right edges at mid-height. In the gap a WebGL dome of fifteen or so small project thumbnails, mostly black and white, tilts in perspective like tiles on a sphere. Nothing else is on the screen.

The heading is broken into an ampersand alone in the left margin and two words stepped over three lines with a hyphen break and a growing indent. Below it a four-column table at 11px: year, site name, awarding body, award. Hairline rules sit under every row, columns align to the hero's band, and year groups are separated by a blank row.

The closing sentence is stepped over four lines with shifting indents, right of centre. To its left two tiny grey captions and an email address at 11px. Under it three 36px outlined circles with social initials, centred, then the handle at about 44px centred on the bottom edge with tiny legal text in the two corners.

steal: Draw one 1px vertical rule and typeset a large sentence around it, alternating words to either side so the line becomes the text's spine.
Split the logotype into two words, ghost them at about 10% grey, and fix one in each bottom corner of the viewport.
Leave the top half of the hero blank and start the name at 50% height so the headline runs off the fold and pulls the scroll.

references.name: Léo Parpeix - Portfolio 2026
references.idea: A soft clay-rendered 3D world, a smiling flower in a sunlit gallery and a bee you can feed, carries the designer's personality while the type stays blunt and heavy.
references.hero: Opens on an empty off-white field with one object: a nearly square card about 28% of the viewport wide, centred, with rounded corners and tilted in 3D perspective, showing a grainy beige render of a smiling clay flower in front of a gridded window. There is no text at all. The card then scales up and flattens into a full-bleed 3D gallery room (flower on a plinth, pale wood floor, sky through tall windows) with a one-line 14px nav laid over it: name far left, role about one-eighth across, three links and a dots menu far right.
references.type: One family (digest name 'text') does everything: 14px regular for nav, captions and metadata, about 24px for intro sentences, and a bold geometric uppercase at 6 to 11vw with leading near 0.9 for centred three-line statements. Almost nothing sits between caption size and display size.
references.colour: #f7f7f7 #0d2a1c #e3d9ca #babeb7 #f6e016 #000000 — Off-white ground with display type in a near-black bottle green rather than black. The 3D scenes are beige and sky blue; the bee's yellow is the only saturated note; one later section turns fully yellow.
references.imagery: Custom clay-like 3D renders with film grain (flower, plinths, bee) and case-study mock-ups of laptops shot on stone or steel. Project images are square-cornered and laid edge to edge in a horizontal strip, with neighbours cut off by the viewport.
references.layout: Alternates full-bleed 3D, centred giant type on blank off-white, and an editorial block where intro text starts past the midpoint and the left half stays empty. The project strip bleeds off both edges; metadata sits beneath in widely spaced small columns.

sections.description: Blank off-white screen with three centred lines of bold uppercase in bottle green, each about 6vw tall with tight leading, the block about 60% of the viewport wide. A small glossy 3D bee hovers over the first line, overlapping the letters, with a soft grey shadow blob cast onto the second line. A tiny parenthesised instruction at 10px sits centred under the block. Nothing else on screen.

Text begins around 55% across: a three-line sentence at about 24px, then two short paragraphs at 14px indented further right, with an asterisk hanging alone in the margin to their left. A white square card carrying a stacked two-line logo sits at the far right, top-aligned with the sentence. The whole left half of the screen stays empty.

Under a small sentence-case label, a horizontal strip of images spans the full viewport: one wide central image, about 73% of the width, flanked by narrow slivers of the previous and next slides cropped by the edges, with 10px gaps. Below, one row of 12 to 14px metadata: index number and client far left, year at centre, team and roles in a right-hand column, and an underlined project link lower left.

Full-screen off-white closing. Three centred lines of the same bold uppercase green type at about 11vw fill three-quarters of the width, with the bee and its detached shadow floating above the first line. A single line of tiny text runs along the bottom edge: credits left, three contact links separated by bullets at centre, copyright right.

steal: Start with one small tilted card on an empty page and scale it into the full-bleed hero scene, so loader and hero are the same object.
Set display type in a near-black green instead of black; it still reads as ink but ties the type to the imagery.
Let a small 3D mascot overlap giant flat type and cast a soft shadow onto it to give a purely typographic screen depth.
